title: The Hare and the Tortoise
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Hare was one day making fun of a Tortoise for being so slow upon his feet. "Wait a bit," said the Tortoise; "I'll run a race with you, and I'll wager that I win." "Oh, well," replied the Hare, who was much amused at the idea, "let's try and see"; and it was soon agreed that the fox should set a course for them, and be the judge. When the time came both started off together, but the Hare was soon so far ahead that he thought he might as well have a rest: so down he lay and fell fast asleep. Meanwhile the Tortoise kept plodding on, and in time reached the goal. At last the Hare woke up with a start, and dashed on at his fastest, but only to find that the Tortoise had already won the race.
Slow and steady wins the race.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who was the Hare making fun of at the start?
options: A Fox
Another Hare
A Tortoise
A Snail

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Tortoise challenge the Hare to do?
options: Run a race with him
Climb a hill together
Carry a heavy stone
Cross a river first

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who is asked to set the course and judge the race?
options: A passing bird
The Tortoise's family
A village elder
The fox

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hare do once he is far ahead in the race?
options: He turns back to check on the Tortoise
He lies down and falls asleep
He stops to eat some grass
He runs even faster to the goal

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Tortoise do while the Hare is resting?
options: He waits for the Hare to wake up
He asks the fox for help
He keeps plodding on toward the goal
He turns around and goes home

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Hare wake up?
options: With a start
Slowly and calmly
Because the Tortoise calls to him
Because the fox wakes him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Hare decide to stop and rest during the race?
options: He is too tired to continue at all
He wants to let the Tortoise catch up out of kindness
The fox tells him to wait for the Tortoise
He believes he is so far ahead that a rest cannot cost him the race

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Tortoise's steady pace, set against the Hare's nap, suggest about winning the race?
options: Only the fastest runner can ever win a race
Steady, unbroken effort can beat a faster but interrupted one
Judges usually favor the slower competitor
Racing is decided by luck rather than effort

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "plodding" describe about the way the Tortoise moves?
options: Hopping quickly in short bursts
Stopping every few steps to rest
Moving slowly but steadily onward
Running as fast as possible

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A faster competitor can still lose by growing careless
Judges should never be chosen from among the animals racing
Races are best settled by starting at different times
A Hare and a Tortoise can never truly be friends

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Tortoise wager when he challenges the Hare?
options: That the fox will change his mind
That the Hare will fall asleep
That the race will end in a tie
That he will win the race

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Hare react to the Tortoise's challenge?
options: He refuses to race at all
He is much amused and agrees to race
He demands a longer course
He asks the Tortoise to go first

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hare do right after he wakes up?
options: He gives up and walks off the course
He asks the Tortoise what happened
He dashes on at his fastest
He goes back to sleep again

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the race's outcome surprising given how it began?
options: The Hare had built up a wide lead before falling asleep
The Tortoise was declared the winner before the race began
The fox refused to let the Hare finish the race
Neither animal wanted to finish the race at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Hare's mockery of the Tortoise at the start reveal about him?
options: He is secretly afraid of losing to the Tortoise
He has raced the Tortoise many times before
He believes the Tortoise is not fit to race at all
He underestimates a competitor because of his slow pace

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does the Tortoise mean when he says he will "wager" that he wins?
options: He is asking for a fair start
He is willing to bet on the outcome
He is warning the Hare to be careful
He is measuring the length of the course

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Tortoise asks a fox to postpone the race
A Hare and a Tortoise agree that the race was unfair
A confident Hare loses a race to a slow but steady Tortoise
A Tortoise gives up early and lets the Hare win
